cohort: 1176 birthing person-infant pairs from the New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study (2010-2017)
finding: Higher birthing person age, education, parity, being married, excessive gestational weight gain, and older gestational age at delivery were associated with better breastfeeding outcomes, while smoking, obesity, and cesarean delivery were negatively associated with breastfeeding outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was negatively associated with breastfeeding outcomes.
